{"type":"text","timestamp":1794693815938,"sessionID":"ses_e23eb5304ffehwW3FZpGB33Om5","part":{"id":"prt_1dc16591a001Meh347Zv8Lp0mH","messageID":"msg_1dc163767001BlZSQyfpZ2aa3g","sessionID":"ses_e23eb5304ffehwW3FZpGB33Om5","type":"text","text":"The shift is over, and all four customer-facing services had a 0% error rate from minute 84 to minute 120. I found and fixed four causes, then a fifth that started during the shift. The two worst outages ran from before the page until about minute 53, and the new one from minute 56 to about minute 82.\n\n1. **fraud-svc had a memory leak from deploy v174.** Memory sat at 99%, the process kept crashing and restarting, and callers' retries overloaded it. That took down web-storefront and admin-portal (about 98% errors). I rolled back v174 at minute 7 and turned on a 60% throttle to stop the retries. Memory dropped to 0.43.\n2. **A config change to push-svc (cfg-16) set its rate limit to 50 per second instead of 5000.** It started 9 minutes before the page. fraud-svc calls push-svc and retries failures, so push-svc was stuck at about 93% errors. That kept the two storefronts down after the fraud-svc fix. I first throttled it to 75%; the overload eased, but the logs showed the rate limiter was still rejecting requests. I reverted the config at minute 46, then lifted both throttles by minute 53, and both storefronts recovered.\n3. **Deploy v39 on suggest-svc had a deadline bug.** It divided the time budget by 10000 instead of 1000, so calls timed out. mobile-api, which earns $22,500 a minute, was losing about 4.5% of requests. suggest-svc was close to capacity, so I added replicas (4 to 6) before rolling back, so the retries the rollback triggers would not overload it. I rolled back at minute 31; mobile-api was at 0% by minute 46. I then set suggest-svc back to 4 replicas, which is free.\n4. **New fault at minute 56: risk-db config change cfg-11.** It removed `currency` from the price fields. Callers' retries then overloaded risk-db, and the two storefronts went to roughly 73–93% errors again. I reverted the config at minute 76 and throttled it to 60% for a few minutes. By minute 79 the retries were gone, so I lifted the throttle at minute 82.\n\n**Costs besides lost revenue:**\n- I didn't restart anything or apply a mitigation that wasn't needed, so there are no $10,000 charges.\n- The two extra suggest-svc replicas ran from about minute 28 to 50, roughly $130.\n- No throttles are left on.\n\n**What I'd do differently:** I spent about 15 minutes throttling push-svc before reading its logs and finding the bad config. Reading the logs first would have brought the storefronts back sooner.","time":{"start":1794693814554,"end":1794693815936}}}
